item.title: Lack of Street lighting around Peckham library, 7th October
item.description:
The lighting around Peckham Library and Peckham Square, particularly along the paths beside the library building and the seating areas in the square, has been consistently dim/ non- existent for several months. Several of the overhead lights appear not to be working, and the overall illumination is too low for safe visibility after dark. Some patches are in complete darkness. The lack of/ low lighting makes it difficult for pedestrians to see clearly, and the area feels unsafe in the evenings. This is a high‑footfall public space used by residents, students, and families, so good lighting is important for safety and accessibility - to deter crime and help us feel safe. Location: Peckham Library, 122 Peckham Hill Street, SE15 5JR — specifically the pedestrian areas surrounding the library building and Peckham Square. The lighting has been insufficient for at least several months, and individual lights appear to have been out for a similar period. Now winter is coming it’s an even bigger issue.
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Peckham Square, Peckham, Greater London
